Estimate Basic Solar-Radiation Parameters

Source: R/env_data_collection_src.R
param_radiation.Rd

Computes extraterrestrial radiation, daylength and actual sunshine duration from day of year and latitude, following FAO-56.

Usage

param_radiation(
  env.data,
  day.id = "DOY",
  latitude = "LAT",
  solarRadiation = NULL,
  merge = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

env.data

data.frame. A get_weather output or equivalent.

day.id

character. Column holding day of year. Default "DOY".

latitude

character. Column holding latitude. Default "LAT".

solarRadiation

character. Column holding incoming shortwave radiation. Default "ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN".

merge

boolean. Bind results onto env.data. Default TRUE.

verbose

boolean. Print a summary of what was computed.

Value

A data.frame with n (actual sunshine hours), N (daylength, h) and RTA (extraterrestrial radiation, MJ/m2/day).

Details

Daylength uses Forsythe et al. (1995), consistent with get_weather. The two functions previously used different formulas that disagreed by up to 0.5 h at high latitude.

The sunset hour angle is clamped so polar day/night yields 0 rather than NaN. Missing radiation is median-imputed within the supplied data, and n is bounded to [0, N].

See also

param_atmospheric, param_temperature, processWTH

Author

Germano Costa Neto

Examples

# \donttest{
env.data <- get_weather(lat = -13.05, lon = -56.05)
#> ---------------------------------------------------------------
